newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS-flat, sifting through payrolls.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS-flat, sifting through payrolls.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices mostly were flat in early afternoon trade on Friday, as the market sifted through the payrolls data for April, which raised eyebrows because some of it seemed a bit contradictory.
"The numbers are not idiot-proof this time," a trader said."
Companies only added 142,000 jobs in April, sharply below the consensus forecast for 211,000 jobs, but the jobless rate fell to 4.9 percent, the lowest rate since 1973.
"Four-point nine percent in an economy is pretty interesting," a trader said, noting that the ramifications of such a low rate would take time to sort out.

Activity was subdued, and although a few bid-wanted lists were being circulated, traders said no particular insights into how customers were positioning themselves could be gleaned from the advertisements, as the bonds being offered were too varied.
Recent buyers of New York City paper have fared well, as long bonds offered in a $701 million sale early this week by the Municipal Water Finance Authority are up around five to seven basis points.

And an approximately $930 million sale of airport bonds by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey last Friday, which was described as a blow-out by some traders, though they noted the debt was sold before the market's big move this week, have chalked up gains of nearly 20 basis points.

While the market has rallied over one point this week as several crucial economic reports suggested the economy was growing without setting off inflation, another supportive factor--hopes a balanced budget soon would be agreed--faded slightly.
A House of Representatives Republican source said that the current difficulty in reaching an agreement had to with a White House request for additional spending.

Still, President Bill Clinton said on Friday he was optimistic about the chances for an accord with Congress to balance the budget by 2002, but insisted tax cuts not be allowed to "explode" the deficit afterwards.
In the debt markets, June municipal futures eased two ticks to 114-20/32, while Treasury bonds fell three ticks to 109-18/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 162 ticks.
In the secondary market, Port Authority of New York and New Jersey Special Project Bonds of December 2022, which pay a 5.75 percent coupon, NET, were bid at 5.94 percent, down three basis points.
Texas State Turnpike Authority Dallas North Thruway Revenues of January 2025, which pay a five percent coupon, were bid at 5.74 percent, NET, unchanged.
